\[
(-1,6),\quad (6,6),\quad (-1,-2),\quad (6,-2).
\]

Choose the diagonal with endpoints \((-1,6)\) and \((6,-2)\). Using the midpoint formula:
\[
\left(\frac{-1+6}{2},\frac{6+(-2)}{2}\right)
=\left(\frac{5}{2},2\right).
\]

Thus, the diagonals intersect at  
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{5}{2},\,2\right)}
\]
